positive_controls.argument: Architecture analysis identifies coupling, persistent-state transitions and shared failure domains that determine whether a proposed canary is actually isolated and what must be qualified before exposure.
Actual-state reconciliation binds observations to the relevant deployed versions and environments, exposing drift or mixed configuration that would invalidate the canary interpretation.
The qualified envelope, representative-configuration limits and change triggers bound where live exposure is permissible and when new pre-exposure evidence is required.
Hazard analysis identifies permissible exposure, relevant adverse signals and necessary prevention or containment, rejecting live experiments where their consequence is unacceptable.
Actual operator, procedure, support, data and contingency readiness determines which stages can proceed and who can stop or expand the transition.
Representative recovery tests, state reconciliation and resource/time limits determine whether the proposed rollback claim is credible and which exposure limit can be supported.
Fleet configuration, support capability, compatibility horizons and retirement obligations identify eligible cohorts and conditions under which old and new versions can coexist.
The multidimensional consequence and commitment profile selects whether canarying, simulation, a qualified pilot, a staged physical transition or no live experiment is appropriate.
Rejecting the universal phase rule prevents early-versus-late timing from replacing examination of actual cohort, state, exposure and recovery costs.
